messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 P1 Alert — toolcall parser errors spike for customer Silverpine (VPC: us-west-2, dedicated-pool: dp-42). Error rate 18% over last 5m, 502/400s returned from function-calling path. Paging oncall.
Sam Turner: I’m on it, pulling logs now. tagging @Maria @Ajay. Could be schema drift from their latest client.
Maria Chavez: Reproduced in logs — parsing failures originate in parser-service v2.3.1 that was rolled ~3h ago as part of internal patch. Only affecting tenant silverpine-*.
Ajay Patel: Confirming isolation: only DP-42 tenants show errors, nothing in hosted API. Likely a parser regression targeting a stricter JSON shape.
Sam Turner: Quick impact note for the page: Silverpine document-generation pipeline failing for ~20% of requests, some automated claims timed out. Customer SE pinged, told them we’re investigating.
Maria Chavez: Sample error from parser logs:
```
ERROR parser: mismatch schema: expected fields [tools[].params] to be object, got string at path tools[0].params.body
payload: {"tool":"extract_claim","params":"{\"text\":\"...\"}"}
stack: parser/handler.go:123
```
Sam Turner: That looks like client started sending serialized JSON inside a string field — schema drift. But why only this tenant? They recently switched to a custom SDK version that bundles tools differently.
Ajay Patel: Checked gateway logs — request headers include X-Client-SDK: silverpine-sdk/3.0.1. That SDK encodes nested tool params as escaped strings. Parser v2.3.1 expects raw objects; previous parser v2.2 tolerated both.
Emily Wong: Suggest two immediate mitigations: 1) route Silverpine to parser v2.2 (roll back for their tenant) OR 2) enable tolerant-parsing feature-flag for dp-42. Which is fastest?
Sam Turner: Rolling back parser for a single dedicated-pool is straightforward via deploy-override. I can pin dp-42 to parser:v2.2 for now. Will also add temporary request-massaging middleware.
Maria Chavez: While Sam works on rollback, I'll craft a compatibility shim we can hotpatch into parser to unescape stringified params. Small change, but riskier than rollback.
ops-bot: runbook check: rollback single-pool parser image: `redwoodctl pool set-image --pool dp-42 --service parser --image parser:v2.2` (requires infra-ops approval).
Sam Turner: Executing rollback now. `redwoodctl` issued, image change started. Watching pods: 
```
kubectl -n dp-42 get pods -l app=parser -w
# rolling update in progress
```
Maria Chavez: I’ll open a canary verification in the staging replica used for dp-42 before we finish.
Ajay Patel: While we wait, temporary customer-facing mitigation: disable function-calling for Silverpine via feature-flag so they get degraded but consistent behavior (less data loss). Command: `featurectl set --tenant silverpine --ff return_no_toolcall true`
Sam Turner: Applied feature-flag. Confirmed 5m post-flag error-rate dropped from 18% -> 2%. Latency improved from ~4.8s to ~1.2s for degraded path.
Emily Wong: Customer update: "We've applied a temporary mitigation and are rolling their traffic to parser v2.2. Will follow up with postmortem and timeline to support SDK fix." SE acknowledged.
ops-bot: parser rollout to dp-42 completed at 1790123520, 8 pods restarted, image parser:v2.2.
Maria Chavez: Canary verification logs show that previously failing payload now parsed correctly:
```
INFO parser: parsed tools[0].params as object
parsed: {"tool":"extract_claim","params":{"body":{"text":"..."}}}
```
Sam Turner: Metrics check: error-rate for Silverpine back down to baseline (<0.5%). Confirming tenant isolation prevented wider blast radius.
Ajay Patel: Post-incident next steps: 1) blocklist sdk version silverpine-sdk/3.0.1 on gateway with soft-block and notify customer to upgrade to 3.0.2 that sends objects not strings; 2) add tolerant-parsing fallback in parser v2.4 that can accept stringified params; 3) strengthen deploy gating so parser minor bump validates tenant SDK compatibility for dedicated pools.
Maria Chavez: I'll take ownership of tolerant-parsing work and a short-lived compatibility middleware that we can promote. Will open PR with tests against both representations.
Emily Wong: I'll own customer comms + timeline and coordinate with SE. Drafting email: immediate mitigation, rollback performed, ETA for permanent fix 48h pending SDK update.
Sam Turner: Handoff note for night oncall (Emily): monitor dp-42 for 12h, watch error-rate and latency, check for any further rollouts from infra that might reintroduce v2.3.1. If errors >2% for 10m, escalate to Eng-ML and SRE.
Emily Wong: Got it. Adding escalations and runbook steps to the thread so night oncall can action.
Sam Turner: Incident severity: P1 (customer-impacting, dedicated pool). Root cause preliminary: parser regression incompatible with a subset of client SDKs -> schema drift.
Maria Chavez: Logging notes for postmortem: capture request samples, gateway headers, parser pod images, rollout history, and the diff between v2.2 and v2.3 parsers relating to JSON decoding.
Ajay Patel: I opened incident ticket INC-2026-412 with RCA owner Maria and action items.
ops-bot: oncall-handoff scheduled: Sam -> Emily at 1790124000 UTC.
Emily Wong: I'll take it from here. Thanks all for quick action. Adding followups: customer SDK advisory, permanent parser fix, deploy gating, and a test matrix for future parser releases.
Sam Turner: Thanks team. Filing quick blameless notes and will add logs to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
Maria Chavez: PR and ticket links will go into the postmortem doc later.
Emily Wong: Closing the live thread; will reopen if regression reappears.
